answers.explanation: ARP maps a neighbor's IPv4 address to the MAC address a frame needs.
The asker doesn't know the target's MAC yet, so it asks everyone.
The reply is unicast, straight back to the host that asked.
arp -a. On Linux, ip neigh shows the same table.
ARP only works within the LAN. The frame goes to the router, which forwards the packet onward.
The target didn't answer: it's switched off, gone, or ignoring ARP.
A packet to the subnet broadcast IP must reach every host, so the frame is a broadcast too.
No manufacturer assigned them, so there's no vendor to find.
VRRP lets routers share one virtual gateway IP and MAC, so a failover doesn't break anyone's ARP cache.
An attacker claims the gateway's IP and becomes a man-in-the-middle.
The switch checks ARP replies against a trusted table of IP-to-MAC bindings and drops lies.
